title: A member a receiver does not know is ignored, at any depth
notes: PROTOCOL.md §4.1 makes forward compatibility a rule: a receiver MUST ignore a member it does not know, at any depth, in either direction, so that a later wire version can add one without breaking this one. This transcript drives the client-to-server direction, which is the half a wire vector can: a `session.hello` and a `doc.open` each carry an unknown top-level member and unknown members nested inside `params`, and both are answered as if the extras were not there — their presence changes nothing in the reply, and neither a `session.error` nor an error response appears. The hello also claims a capability name the server cannot know, which §10 says is ignored the same way. The server-to-client direction is a receiver obligation a transcript cannot pin, since the reference server never emits a member outside `selvage/1`.
